title: Long byte keys as position alphabets on LP2
question: Do five specified source byte streams serve as synchronized substitution-alphabet labels for LP2?
reader_question: Could these byte streams select the alphabet at each rune?
summary: Exact Stage W replay finds no hit among 50 long-byte-key/section settings; 12 are excluded by powered controls and 38 remain untestable under the source rule.
finding: The source's negative-control gate passes. No LP2 setting reaches its +30-nat threshold; all five positive controls detect 12 settings, while 38 lack that power. The best LP2 score is 0.84 nats, below threshold.
limitations: The model requires the named byte key to remain in step with each tested rune stream, with a fixed one-to-one substitution for every byte value. Short settings without detected positive controls are untestable; key skips, other phase rules and layered transformations remain open.
next_steps: Any different key or resynchronization rule needs its own declared alignment and same-length positive and flat-negative controls before drawing a negative conclusion.

scope.representation: Canonical GP29 rune streams for each unsolved marked section 7–15 and the joined LP2-00–55 stream; five byte keys from the source hint file, its reversal and three source byte files. The three files' puzzle-payload provenance was not independently verified.
scope.procedure: Replay the pinned Stage S LP2 dependency for these same 50 cells, then run unchanged Stage W source with its aligned controls; independently verify all control counts, phase bounds, source-score agreement and verdict rules.
scope.parameters: Five key classings × ten section alignments; all source key phases; five same-length positives and five flat negatives per cell, plus one shuffled-key LP2 null per key; anti-doublet keep 0.19; source score threshold +30 nats.
scope.exclusions: Other source Stage S classings, alternate byte encodings, offsets beyond source phases, key skips/restarts, changing alphabets, other plaintext distributions and composed ciphers.

review.kind: exact public-source Stage W replay with independent control/verdict check
review.reviewer: Both Stage W tables reproduced byte-for-byte against pinned published source; all 50 Stage S dependency rows agree with pinned full table; 505 controls and 50 decisions independently checked

reproduction.environment: Bundled checks use Python 3 standard library. Optional full pinned-source replay requires NumPy and an external source checkout.

visuals.caption: Powered exclusions out of ten alignments per byte key. File 17/21/43 are source file names, not LP2 page numbers; unresolved settings lacked positive-control power.
